answer: SybilGuard employs a three-step mechanism: 1) Users deposit 100 tokens into a central lagoon. 2) Identity creation requires staking an additional 50 tokens in a time-locked inlet. 3) Slashing of the inlet stake occurs for malicious activity, returning it to the lagoon. Cost for N identities: $50 \times N$. Failure occurs if one entity acquires 1000 identities. This is as if a single basalt column could block the entire inlet.
